A: Both handle SEO basics well, including titles, descriptions, redirects and structured data. Webflow hosting is generally fast by default, while WordPress speed depends on host, theme and plugins. Content quality, structure and page speed matter more than which platform you choose.

Q: Can I move a Webflow site to another host?
A: Only partly. Webflow allows some code export, but dynamic CMS features do not export in a working form, so leaving the platform usually means rebuilding the site. WordPress sites can be moved, with code and database, to any host whenever you choose.

Q: Is it easy to find Webflow developers in Pakistan?
A: There are Webflow specialists in Pakistan, but the pool is much smaller than for WordPress, which has a very large number of developers and agencies. This affects choice, availability and ease of replacing a developer later, so consider it before deciding.

Q: Can I pay for Webflow from Pakistan?
A: Webflow bills in US dollars by international card, so you need a card enabled for foreign online payments and you take on exchange rate changes each year. WordPress hosting can be paid in rupees through Pakistani providers, which some businesses find simpler.

Q: WordPress lein ya Webflow?
A: Agar design par zyada zor hai aur dollar mein payment masla nahin to Webflow theek hai. Agar code aur data apne paas chahiye, rupay mein hosting, Pakistan mein asani se developer, ya local payment wala online store chahiye to WordPress behtar hai. Dono SEO ke liye theek hain.

## Wix vs WordPress for a Pakistani Business: Ownership, Payments, SEO and Cost
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/wix-vs-wordpress
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: In Wix vs WordPress, Wix is easier to start: drag-and-drop editing, hosting included and a monthly plan paid by card. WordPress takes more set-up but gives full ownership, rupee hosting options, more flexibility and a large local developer pool. For a simple brochure site you edit yourself, Wix is fine; for growth, WordPress usually wins over 3 years.
Key points:
- Wix is a hosted builder; your site lives on Wix's platform.
- WordPress can be hosted anywhere, including on Pakistani hosting billed in rupees.
- Wix plans are paid by international card; prices and currency vary by location.
- Local payment gateways and complex features are usually easier on WordPress.
- Both can rank in search; content, structure and speed matter more.

Q: Is Wix or WordPress better for a small business in Pakistan?
A: Wix suits a simple site you build and edit yourself quickly, paid by international card. WordPress suits businesses wanting full ownership, rupee hosting, local payment gateways, growth and easy access to local developers. Over three years, WordPress usually gives more flexibility for growing businesses.

Q: How much does Wix cost in Pakistan?
A: Wix's official plans page lists a free plan and four premium plans, Light, Core, Business and Business Elite, priced for yearly subscriptions. It states that prices and currency vary by location, so check the figures shown to you on the page before deciding.

Q: Is it possible to move a Wix site to WordPress?
A: Not directly. Wix sites run only on Wix's platform, so moving usually means rebuilding the design on WordPress and copying content across. Keep copies of your text and images, and register your domain in your own name, so the move is simpler if you decide later.

Q: Is Wix good for SEO?
A: Wix handles many technical SEO basics automatically and lets you set titles, descriptions and redirects, so it can rank. WordPress offers finer control through plugins and custom code as sites grow. On both, content quality, structure and page speed matter most.

Q: Can I accept JazzCash or Easypaisa on Wix?
A: It depends on Wix's current list of supported payment providers, which may not include the Pakistani gateway or wallet you want. Check Wix's official payment provider list before building. WordPress with WooCommerce generally offers more local gateway options through plugins.

Q: Is WordPress free?
A: The WordPress software is free and open source. You still pay for hosting, a domain, any premium theme or plugins and maintenance, either your own time or a developer's. These costs can be paid in rupees through Pakistani hosting providers.

Q: Wix lein ya WordPress?
A: Agar jaldi aur saada website chahiye jo aap khud bana aur badal sakein, aur card se dollar mein payment ho sakti hai, to Wix theek hai. Agar website apni malkiyat mein chahiye, rupay mein hosting, local payment ya aage barhne ki gunjaish chahiye to WordPress behtar hai.

## Free Website vs Paid Website: What a Pakistani Business Really Gives Up With a Free Site
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/free-website-vs-paid-website
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: A free website vs paid website choice: free usually means a platform subdomain, platform branding, limited features and no ownership; paid gives your own domain, branding and room to grow. Free suits testing an idea, but a business wanting trust needs at least its own domain, from Rs 2,100 a year for .pk.
Key points:
- Free sites usually live on a subdomain, such as yourname.platform.com, which looks less professional.
- Free plans typically show the platform's branding and limit features.
- Your own domain is the single most important upgrade, and it is inexpensive.
- A free site is fine for testing an idea or a personal project.
- Whatever you start with, keep copies of your content so you can move later.

Q: Is a free website good enough for a business?
A: For testing an idea, a personal portfolio or a temporary event, yes. For a business that needs customers' trust, online payments, business email or search visibility, a free site usually holds it back, mainly because of the platform subdomain, platform branding and limited features.

Q: What is the main disadvantage of a free website?
A: Usually the web address. Free sites typically live on a platform subdomain, such as username.wixsite.com/sitename on Wix, and show the platform's branding. This looks less established, is harder to remember and cannot be used for business email on your own domain.

Q: How much does my own domain cost in Pakistan?
A: PKNIC lists .pk domains at Rs 2,100 a year for Pakistan-based registrants from 1 August 2026, billed for a two-year period. Other extensions such as .com have their own prices set by registrars. Owning your domain is usually the most valuable first upgrade.

Q: Can I use my own domain with a free website builder?
A: Usually not on a fully free plan. Most builders require a paid plan to connect your own domain and remove their branding. Check the builder's official plans page, and compare that cost with a simple self-hosted site on your own domain and hosting.

Q: Is Google Sites a good free business website?
A: Google Sites is free and simple, and it suits internal or very basic pages. It offers limited design, features and search optimisation control compared with a proper website. For a customer-facing business site, a simple paid site on your own domain usually serves you better.

Q: How do I move from a free website to a paid one?
A: Keep copies of your text and images outside the platform, build the new site on your own domain, add a notice and link on the old site if the platform allows, and update your Google Business Profile, social media and printed materials to the new address.

Q: Kya muft website business ke liye kaafi hai?
A: Kisi idea ko test karne ya personal kaam ke liye muft website theek hai. Business ke liye apna domain, jaise yourbusiness.pk, bohat zaroori hai kyunke is se bharosa barhta hai aur business email bhi ban sakti hai. .pk domain PKNIC ke mutabiq Rs 2,100 salana hai.

## Custom Code vs No Code: What a Business Owner Should Choose for a Website or App
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/custom-code-vs-no-code-website
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: In custom code vs no code, no-code tools win on speed and upfront cost for simple sites, internal tools and early prototypes. Custom code wins when you need unusual features, scale, performance, full ownership or freedom to switch providers. Compare 3-year costs: our custom web apps fall within Rs 360,000 to Rs 1,350,000, while no-code tools charge monthly.
Key points:
- No-code tools are excellent for testing ideas and building simple tools quickly.
- Their limits show up with complex logic, heavy traffic, integrations and data volumes.
- Lock-in is the main long-term risk: moving off a no-code platform usually means rebuilding.
- Monthly no-code fees add up; compare totals over three years, not month one.
- Many businesses prototype in no-code, then rebuild in custom code once the idea is proven.

Q: Should I choose custom code or no-code for my business?
A: Choose no-code to test ideas, build simple internal tools or launch a basic marketing site quickly and cheaply. Choose custom code when the product is central to your business, needs complex logic or integrations, must scale, or must be fully owned and portable.

Q: What are the limitations of no-code apps?
A: Common limits are complex business logic, integrations with local payment gateways or your own systems, performance at higher user numbers, data volume, design flexibility and portability. Monthly fees can also rise sharply as usage grows. Check limits on each platform's official documentation.

Q: Is no-code cheaper than custom development?
A: At the start, usually yes. Over three years it depends on growth. Add platform fees at the tier you will need, usage charges and specialist help, then compare with a custom build within our Rs 360,000 to Rs 1,350,000 range plus hosting and maintenance.

Q: What is no-code lock-in?
A: Lock-in means your app's logic and screens exist only in the platform's format. If prices rise, features change or the platform closes, moving usually means rebuilding from scratch. Export data regularly and document how the app works to reduce this risk.

Q: Can I start on no-code and switch to custom code later?
A: Yes, and many businesses do. Use no-code to test whether customers want the product, then rebuild the proven version in custom code. Plan for a rebuild rather than a migration, because no-code apps rarely convert directly into clean, maintainable code that developers can extend.

Q: Who maintains a no-code app?
A: Trained staff or no-code specialists can usually make changes without developers, which is a real advantage. Complex apps still need careful structure and documentation, otherwise they become hard to change. Custom code needs developers, but can be maintained by any competent team.

Q: No code ya custom code, kya behtar hai?
A: Idea test karne, chhote andaruni tools ya saada website ke liye no-code jaldi aur sasta hai. Agar app aap ke business ka markaz hai, pechida kaam, local payment ya bohat se users chahiye, ya code apne paas rakhna hai, to custom code behtar hai. Teen saal ka kul kharch zaroor milayen.

## Flutter vs React Native, or a PWA: Choosing the Right Route for Your First App
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/flutter-vs-react-native-vs-pwa
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: Flutter vs React Native is a close contest: both build Android and iPhone apps from one codebase, with mature tools and strong hiring pools in Pakistan. Flutter offers consistent design control; React Native suits teams with JavaScript skills. A progressive web app may be enough and skips store fees; Apple charges $99 a year, Google Play $25 once.
Key points:
- Both Flutter and React Native produce Android and iOS apps from one codebase.
- The team's existing skills often matter more than framework differences.
- A progressive web app works in the browser, installs on phones and avoids app store approval.
- App stores charge developer fees: Apple's program is $99 a year; Google Play is a one-time $25.
- Maintenance, store updates and OS changes continue after launch whichever route you choose.

Q: Is Flutter or React Native better for a first app?
A: Both are mature and widely used for apps on Android and iPhone from one codebase. Flutter offers consistent custom design across platforms; React Native uses native components and suits teams already using JavaScript. Your team's skills and design goals usually matter more than framework differences.

Q: What is a progressive web app?
A: A progressive web app is a website built to behave like an app. It runs in the browser, can be added to the home screen, can work offline for some features and receives updates instantly, without app store approval or developer fees for browser installation.

Q: How much are app store developer fees?
A: Apple's enrolment page lists the Apple Developer Program at $99 a year for individuals and organisations, and Google Play's help centre lists a one-time $25 registration fee, both checked 30 October 2026. Prices may appear in local currency during enrolment.

Q: Is a PWA good enough instead of an app?
A: Often, for booking tools, customer portals, ordering systems and internal tools. It is cheaper to build and maintain and avoids store fees. Limits include weaker support for some device features on iPhone and no app store listing, which matters if store discovery is important.

Q: Is it easy to hire Flutter or React Native developers in Pakistan?
A: Yes. Pakistan has strong pools of both Flutter and React Native developers, and any competent web developer can build a PWA. Check portfolios for published apps, ask about testing on real devices and confirm who will handle store submissions and updates.

Q: What does it cost to maintain an app after launch?
A: Apps need updates for new Android and iOS versions, store rule changes, bug fixes and security patches, plus hosting for any back end. Budget for regular maintenance from day one. PWAs are generally simpler to maintain because updates go live instantly in the browser.

Q: Pehli app ke liye Flutter, React Native ya PWA?
A: Flutter aur React Native dono se aik hi code mein Android aur iPhone app banti hai, aur Pakistan mein dono ke developers mil jate hain. Agar zyada phone features nahin chahiye to PWA sasta aur asaan hai, store fees bhi nahin. Apple ki fee $99 salana aur Google Play ki $25 aik baar hai.

## Shopify vs Daraz for Pakistani Sellers: Running Your Own Store and a Daraz Shop Together
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/shopify-vs-daraz-storefront
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: Shopify vs Daraz is rarely either-or. Daraz brings marketplace traffic and handles much of the buying journey; your own Shopify store gives brand control, customer data and repeat sales without marketplace commissions. Many Pakistani sellers run both, with 1 stock count, clear pricing per channel and a daily routine to prevent overselling.
Key points:
- Daraz brings buyers who are already shopping; your own store builds a brand and repeat customers.
- Marketplace sellers do not own the customer relationship in the same way as on their own store.
- One stock count across channels prevents overselling and cancelled orders.
- Prices can differ by channel, but must stay consistent with each channel's rules.
- Start with one channel well, then add the second with a clear process.

Q: Should I sell on Daraz or my own Shopify store?
A: Often both. Daraz brings marketplace shoppers and handles much of the buying journey, while your own store gives brand control, direct customer relationships and repeat sales without marketplace commissions. Start with one channel done well, then add the other with a clear process.

Q: How do I avoid overselling on Daraz and Shopify?
A: Keep one stock count across channels. Options include fixed stock allocations per channel, a master sheet updated after every order, or inventory sync tools that update both channels automatically. Count physical stock regularly and compare it with the system to catch errors early.

Q: Can I charge different prices on Daraz and my own store?
A: Many sellers do, often pricing slightly higher on the marketplace to cover commissions or offering exclusive bundles on their own store. Keep pricing honest, follow each channel's rules on pricing and promotions, and make delivery and cash on delivery terms clear on both.

Q: Do I own customer data from Daraz orders?
A: Marketplace platforms control much of the customer relationship, and their rules limit how sellers may use buyer details, usually to fulfilling orders. On your own store, customer data sits in your account and you can market to customers with their consent.

Q: How much does Shopify cost compared with Daraz?
A: Shopify's pricing page, checked 30 October 2026, lists Basic at $29 a month billed yearly, plus apps and third-party transaction fees in Pakistan. Daraz charges marketplace commissions and fees set in its seller centre, which change, so check its official pages for current figures.

Q: What daily routine helps run two sales channels?
A: Check orders on both channels at fixed times, update or confirm stock immediately, pack and dispatch from one queue labelled by channel, track cancellations and returns per channel, and review profit per channel every month after all fees and charges.

Q: Daraz aur apna Shopify store dono kaise chalayein?
A: Daraz se tayyar customers milte hain aur apne store se brand aur dobara khareedne wale customers bante hain. Dono ka stock aik hi jagah se control karein taake aik cheez do baar na bik jaye. Har roz muqarrar waqt par orders dekhein aur har mahine dono ka munafa alag hisaab karein.

## Your First Website Discovery Meeting: What to Prepare, What We Ask and What You Decide
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-discovery-meeting-what-to-expect
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: A website discovery meeting is a first working session, usually 45 to 90 minutes, where you and the developer agree goals, audience, pages, features, content, budget and timeline. Bring examples you like, your logo, a rough page list, and the questions customers ask most. You should leave with a clear scope and a written quote to follow.
Key points:
- The meeting is about your business goals first, design second.
- Bring examples of sites you like and dislike, with reasons.
- Know your rough budget and deadline; it saves time for both sides.
- Expect questions about customers, content, features and who will maintain the site.
- A written scope and quote should follow, ideally within a few working days.

Q: What happens in a website discovery meeting?
A: You and the developer agree your business goals, audience, pages, features, content responsibilities, budget and timeline. It usually lasts 45 to 90 minutes. A good developer asks many questions about customers and goals before discussing design, and follows up with a written scope and quote.

Q: What should I prepare for my first meeting with a web developer?
A: Bring examples of websites you like and dislike with reasons, your logo and brand colours, a rough page list, the questions customers ask most, details of any current domain and hosting, your budget range and any fixed launch date. A filled-in brief template helps greatly.

Q: What questions will a web designer ask me?
A: Expect questions about what visitors should do on the site, your most important services or products, competitors, languages, payment and courier needs, who will update the site after launch, and who approves designs and content. These shape the scope, timeline and price.

Q: Should I tell the developer my budget?
A: Yes, at least a range. It lets the developer propose a realistic scope instead of guessing, and avoids wasted time on designs you cannot afford. Published price lists also help you match your expectations to typical package costs before the meeting.

Q: Can a website discovery meeting be done online?
A: Yes. Many meetings happen by video call, especially with overseas clients. Share your screen to show examples, and record the call with permission so decisions are not lost. Follow up with written notes listing what was agreed and any open questions.

Q: What should I receive after the discovery meeting?
A: A written scope and quote listing pages, features, timeline, payment milestones, what you must provide and what is excluded. Compare it with your own notes and ask questions before signing. A clear scope prevents disagreements and extra charges later in the project.

Q: Website ki pehli meeting mein kya le kar jayen?
A: Pasandeeda aur napasandeeda websites ki misaalein, apna logo, pages ki andazan list, customers ke aam sawal, maujooda domain aur hosting ki tafseel, aur budget ka andaza saath le jayen. Meeting ke baad likhit scope aur quote zaroor lein aur sign karne se pehle parh lein.

## How to Give Website Design Feedback That Developers Can Actually Use
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/how-to-give-website-design-feedback
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: Good website design feedback is specific, tied to a goal and collected in one place. Say what to change, where and why, using annotated screenshots, and send one consolidated list per round rather than scattered WhatsApp messages. Agree in advance how many revision rounds are included, often 2, and who gives final approval.
Key points:
- Specific comments tied to customers or goals get better results than personal taste.
- Annotated screenshots remove guesswork about which element you mean.
- Collect feedback from everyone, resolve disagreements internally, then send one list.
- Know how many revision rounds your contract includes.
- Approve designs in writing, so the build can start on a fixed basis.

Q: How do I give good website design feedback?
A: Be specific about what to change, where and why, tie comments to your customers or goals rather than personal taste, use annotated screenshots, say whether comments apply to mobile or desktop, and send one consolidated list per round from one person.

Q: How many design revisions are normal for a website?
A: Many contracts include a set number of revision rounds, often two, with extra rounds charged. A round is one consolidated list of comments and one revised design. Check your contract before starting and use rounds for meaningful changes rather than small personal preferences.

Q: Why should feedback come from one person?
A: When several people send separate comments, designers receive contradictions and cannot tell whose view wins, which wastes revision rounds. Collect everyone's input, resolve disagreements internally, then send one agreed list from one named person, ideally the person named in the contract.

Q: Should I review my website design on a phone?
A: Yes, first. Most visitors will see the site on a phone, so check the mobile design on your own device. Make sure text is readable without zooming, buttons are easy to tap and the main call to action is visible without scrolling.

Q: What should I focus on when reviewing a design?
A: Start with clarity, whether visitors understand what you do quickly, then the main call to action on mobile, then accuracy of services, prices and contact details, then trust and authenticity. Leave colours and fonts until last unless they clash with your brand.

Q: How do I approve a website design?
A: Send written approval by email or message once the design is right, stating that it is approved for build. This fixes the design so development can start and makes any later design changes clearly separate, which helps avoid disputes about extra charges.

Q: Website design par raaye kaise dein?
A: Saaf batayein kya badalna hai, kahan aur kyun, aur screenshot par nishan laga kar bhejein. Ghar ke sab logon ki raaye pehle aapas mein tay karein, phir aik hi list aik shakhs bheje. Pehle mobile par design dekhein, aur pasand aane par likh kar approve karein.

## Website Change Requests During a Project: Why They Cost Extra and How to Plan for Them
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-change-requests-cost
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: A website change request is anything added or altered after the scope was agreed: a new page, a new feature, a redesign of an approved section. It costs extra because it adds work and can delay launch. Agree a written process: describe the change, get a quote and new date, approve in writing, then build, with 1 small contingency budget.
Key points:
- Changes are normal; unmanaged changes are what cause disputes.
- Fixed prices cover the agreed scope only; new work needs its own quote.
- Changes after design approval or build often cost more than the same change earlier.
- A simple written change process protects both owner and developer.
- Group small changes into a single request where possible.

Q: What is a website change request?
A: It is any addition or alteration to a website project after the scope was agreed, such as a new page, a new feature, a redesign of an approved section or a new integration. Fixing errors against the agreed scope is not a change request; adding new work is.

Q: Why do website changes cost extra?
A: Because they add work beyond what the agreed price covered, and changes made after design approval or building often mean undoing, redoing and retesting finished work. The later a change comes, the more it usually costs and the more it can delay the launch.

Q: How should change requests be handled?
A: Describe the change in writing, get a written estimate of cost and timeline impact, decide whether to approve, defer or drop it, record approved changes in one list, and only then let building start. This simple process prevents surprises and disputes at the end.

Q: What is scope creep in web development?
A: Scope creep is the gradual growth of a project through small, informal additions that nobody formally prices or schedules. Each request seems minor, but together they delay launch and cause disagreements about cost. A written change process and a phase two list help prevent it.

Q: How can I avoid change requests on my website project?
A: Invest time in the brief and discovery meeting, agree full page and feature lists before design, involve all decision-makers early, keep a phase two list for ideas that can wait, and hold a small contingency budget for genuine surprises during the project.

Q: Are text edits a change request?
A: Usually not, if they fall within the agreed revision rounds and apply to pages already in scope. Adding new sections, rewriting pages after approval or adding new content types may count as changes. Check what your contract says about revisions and content.

Q: Website project ke dauran tabdeeli ka kharch kyun lagta hai?
A: Jo kaam pehle tay hua tha qeemat sirf usi ki hoti hai. Naya page ya feature baad mein maangne se naya kaam aur waqt lagta hai, khaas taur par design approve hone ke baad. Har tabdeeli likh kar bhejein, qeemat aur nayi tareekh poochein, aur approve karne ke baad hi kaam shuru karwayen.

## Website User Acceptance Testing: An Owner's 30-Minute Check Before Sign-Off
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-testing-before-sign-off
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: Website user acceptance testing is the owner's final check that the site works as agreed before sign-off. In about 30 minutes, test it on your own phone, submit every form, place a test order, click every button and link, read every page for errors and check contact details. Report issues in one list, then sign off in writing.
Key points:
- Acceptance testing checks the site against the agreed scope, from a customer's point of view.
- Test on your own phone first, then a computer.
- Submit every form and place a real test order or booking.
- Read every page for wrong prices, numbers and addresses.
- Report issues in one numbered list, and sign off in writing once fixed.

Q: What is website user acceptance testing?
A: It is the owner's final check that a website works as agreed before signing it off and making the final payment. It focuses on what customers experience: layout on phones, forms, buttons, payments or bookings, content accuracy, links and speed. No technical skills are needed.

Q: How long does website acceptance testing take?
A: For a typical small business website, a focused check takes about 30 minutes using a checklist: phone layout, forms, WhatsApp and call buttons, payments or bookings, content accuracy, speed and links. Larger stores or web apps need longer and more structured testing.

Q: What should I test before signing off my website?
A: Check every page on your own phone, submit every form and confirm the emails arrive, tap every WhatsApp and phone button, place test orders or bookings with each payment method, read all prices, addresses and hours, and click menu and footer links.

Q: How should I report problems found during testing?
A: Make one numbered list showing the page, device, what you expected and what happened, with a screenshot for each item. Mark each issue as blocking or minor, and send the list once. Items that were never in scope should be treated as change requests.

Q: When should I make the final payment for my website?
A: After blocking issues found in acceptance testing are fixed and rechecked, and you have confirmed you hold all logins, the domain and hosting are in your name, and a backup exists. Sign off in writing at that point, which usually triggers the final milestone.

Q: Should I use real customer data when testing?
A: No. Use your own details or clearly fake ones for test forms and orders, never real customers' information. Ask the developer to remove test orders, bookings and form entries before launch, so reports and inboxes start clean and no test data is left behind.

Q: Website sign off se pehle kya check karein?
A: Apne phone par har page dekhein, har form bhej kar dekhein ke email aati hai, WhatsApp aur call ke button dabayein, test order ya booking karein, aur qeematein, pata aur auqaat ghaur se parhein. Masail aik list mein bhejein aur theek hone ke baad likh kar sign off karein.

## Website Maintenance Contract Checklist: Response Times, Exclusions, Access and Exit Terms
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-maintenance-contract-checklist
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: A website maintenance contract should list exactly which tasks are included, such as updates, backups, monitoring and a number of small changes, plus response times by severity, what is excluded, who holds access, how backups are restored, how prices can change and how either side can end it. Our care plans start from Rs 7,200 a month.
Key points:
- Vague promises like full support cause disputes; list tasks and limits.
- Response times should differ by severity: site down, feature broken, minor issue.
- You should keep owner-level access to hosting, domain and the website at all times.
- Backups need a stated frequency, storage location and a tested restore.
- Exit terms and handover duties protect you if the relationship ends.

Q: What should a website maintenance contract include?
A: Included tasks, response times by severity, working hours, exclusions, the rate or process for extra work, access and ownership terms, backup frequency and restore tests, monthly reporting, the fee and notice for price changes, and exit terms with a handover of access and documentation.

Q: What response time should I expect from website support?
A: It should depend on severity. A site that is down or a broken checkout needs the fastest response, often within a few working hours, while minor issues may take a few working days. Agree working hours in writing and pay separately for out-of-hours cover if needed.

Q: What is usually excluded from website maintenance?
A: New pages, features and redesigns, content writing and photography, problems caused by third-party outages, damage from uncoordinated changes by others, and licence fees for premium plugins unless the contract includes them. Clear exclusions prevent a care plan becoming unlimited development.

Q: Should my maintenance provider hold my website logins?
A: They should have their own user access, but your business must keep owner-level access to the domain, hosting and website. Never let a provider be the only holder of owner logins, because you could lose control of your site if the relationship ends.

Q: How often should website backups be taken?
A: It depends on how often the site changes. Many small business sites back up daily, while busy online stores may need more frequent backups. The contract should state frequency, storage location off the hosting server, retention period and how often restores are tested.

Q: How do I end a website maintenance contract?
A: Follow the agreed notice period, often one month, then collect a handover: confirmation that the provider's access is removed, documentation of custom work, the latest backup and a list of plugins and licences. Change passwords once the handover is complete.

Q: Website maintenance ka muahida kaise likhwayen?
A: Likh kar tay karein ke kaun se kaam shamil hain, masla hone par kitni der mein jawab milega, kya shamil nahin, extra kaam ka rate kya hai, backup kab aur kahan hoga, aur muahida khatam karne ka tareeqa kya hai. Domain aur hosting ka owner access hamesha apne paas rakhein.

## Why Website Project Delays Happen, and How Owners and Developers Can Stay on Schedule
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-project-delays-why
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: Most website project delays come from 4 causes: content arriving late, slow or scattered feedback, new requests added mid-project, and developers juggling too many projects. Owners can prevent the first three by preparing content early, naming one decision-maker and parking new ideas for phase two. Ask developers for a dated plan with weekly updates.
Key points:
- Late content is the single most common reason websites launch late.
- Every day a design waits for feedback adds a day to the launch.
- New ideas mid-project should go on a phase two list unless they are essential.
- A dated milestone plan and weekly updates expose delays early.
- When a deadline slips, agree a new date in writing and the reason for it.

Q: Why is my website taking so long to build?
A: The most common causes are late content, slow or scattered feedback, new requests added mid-project, missing logins or third-party approvals, and developers handling too many projects at once. Ask for a dated milestone plan and weekly updates to see exactly where the project stands.

Q: What is the biggest cause of website delays?
A: Content arriving late is the single most common cause. Developers can build pages without final text and photos, but cannot launch them. Starting content in week one with a simple template, and accepting good drafts that can improve after launch, prevents most of these delays.

Q: How can I keep my website project on schedule?
A: Name one decision-maker, gather logins early, start content immediately, apply for payment gateways or APIs at the start, agree feedback turnaround times, and keep a phase two list for new ideas. Ask the developer for a dated plan and weekly preview links.

Q: What should I do if my developer misses a deadline?
A: Ask for the cause and agree a new date in writing. If delays on the developer's side keep repeating, refer to the milestone terms in your contract. Avoid simply stopping payment without discussion, because it usually makes delays longer rather than shorter.

Q: Which third-party steps delay website launches?
A: Payment gateway merchant accounts, WhatsApp Business API verification, courier integrations and domain transfers often take longest, because they depend on other companies' processes and documents. Start these applications at the beginning of the project rather than the week before launch.

Q: Should I launch the website before everything is finished?
A: Often, yes. If the core pages, contact options and key features work, launching and adding remaining pages or features later is usually better than waiting months. Agree with the developer what counts as the minimum for launch and what goes into phase two.

Q: Website banne mein der kyun hoti hai?
A: Aksar mawaad aur tasveerein der se milti hain, raaye dene mein waqt lagta hai, ya beech mein naye kaam add ho jate hain. Aik shakhs ko faisla karne wala banayein, pehle hafte se mawaad shuru karein, aur naye idea doosre marhale ke liye rakh lein. Developer se tareekhon wala plan lein.

## How to Manage a Web Developer When You Are Not Technical: Demos, Previews and Plain Reports
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/non-technical-owner-managing-developer
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: To manage a web developer without technical knowledge, judge progress by what you can see: a weekly demo or staging link, a short plain-language report, and milestones tied to visible results and payments. Ask what was done, what is next and what is blocked. Keep 1 shared task list and insist that accounts are in your name.
Key points:
- You do not need to read code; you need to see working results regularly.
- A staging link shows real progress better than any status message.
- Short weekly reports should answer three questions: done, next, blocked.
- Tie payments to milestones you can see and test.
- Keep domain, hosting and code accounts in your business's name.

Q: How do I manage a web developer if I am not technical?
A: Judge progress by what you can see: a staging link, weekly plain-language reports saying what is done, next and blocked, regular short demos, a shared task list, and milestones tied to visible results and payments. Insist that all accounts are in your business's name.

Q: How can I check my developer's progress?
A: Ask for a staging or preview link you can open on your phone, and look for visible changes each week. Combine this with a short written report and a brief demo call. If weeks pass with nothing new on staging, ask direct questions straight away.

Q: What should a weekly developer report include?
A: Three things in plain words: what was completed and where you can see it, what will be worked on next, and anything blocked, including what the developer needs from you. It should also say whether the next milestone date is still realistic.

Q: What is a staging site?
A: A staging site is a private copy of your website in progress, where you can see real pages, click buttons and test forms before launch. It should be password-protected and hidden from search engines, and it is the best way for non-technical owners to track progress.

Q: What are the warning signs of a bad developer?
A: No preview link or one that rarely changes, jargon-heavy reports that never say what is finished, repeated missed dates, requests for money before milestones are delivered, reluctance to put accounts in your name, and long silences followed by a rush near deadlines.

Q: Should I pay my developer upfront?
A: Usually a deposit, then payments tied to milestones you can see and test, such as approved designs, pages built on staging, working features and launch. Paying everything upfront removes your leverage; paying nothing upfront makes it hard for developers to commit time.

Q: Developer se kaam kaise lein agar mujhe technical samajh nahin?
A: Code samajhna zaroori nahin. Developer se staging link lein jo aap phone par dekh sakein, har hafte saada report lein ke kya hua, aage kya hai aur kahan rukawat hai. Payment sirf nazar aane wale kaam par dein, aur domain, hosting aur code ke accounts apne naam par rakhein.

## How to Take Over a Website From a Previous Developer: Access, Audit and First-Week Fixes
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/taking-over-website-from-old-developer
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: To take over a website from a previous developer, first recover owner access to the domain, hosting, website admin and email, then take a full backup, change all passwords and audit the site: software versions, plugins, security, speed and forms. Fix urgent problems in the first week and plan the rest, without rushing a rebuild.
Key points:
- Access comes first: domain, hosting, website admin, email, analytics and DNS.
- Take a full backup before changing anything.
- Change every password and remove the old developer's accounts once access is secure.
- Audit before rebuilding; many inherited sites need fixes, not replacement.
- Document what you find so the next handover is easier.

Q: How do I take over a website from my previous developer?
A: Recover owner access to the domain, hosting, website admin, email, DNS and analytics first. Then take a full backup, change every password, turn on two-step verification, remove the old developer's accounts and audit the site before deciding on fixes or a rebuild.

Q: What if my old developer will not give me the logins?
A: Contact the domain registrar, hosting company and email provider directly with proof of ownership, such as invoices, business documents or billing records. They have recovery processes. If the domain is registered in the developer's name, check your contract and take advice.

Q: What should a new developer check on an inherited website?
A: Software and plugin versions, abandoned or pirated plugins, signs of malware, whether forms deliver messages, mobile speed, existing backups and whether they restore, Search Console errors, and whether any custom code is documented and understood well enough for another developer to maintain it.

Q: Should I rebuild a website I inherited from another developer?
A: Not automatically. Rebuild if the site runs on an abandoned platform, is heavily hacked, cannot be updated or no longer fits the business. Otherwise, a cleaned-up, updated site may serve well for years. Decide after a proper audit rather than before.

Q: What should be fixed first on a taken-over website?
A: Anything that risks losing data, customers or access: missing backups, critical security updates, broken forms, expiring certificates or domains, and malware. Design, speed and content improvements can follow calmly, in a planned order, once the site is stable and secure again.

Q: What about customer data my old developer still has?
A: Ask the previous developer in writing to delete any copies of your database, customer data or backups, and to confirm deletion. If you believe customer data was exposed or misused, take advice promptly on your obligations to the customers and other people affected.

Q: Purane developer se website kaise wapas lein?
A: Sab se pehle domain, hosting, website admin aur email ka owner access hasil karein. Phir poora backup lein, tamam passwords badlein, purane developer ke accounts hata dein aur website ka audit karwayen. Pehle hafte sirf zaroori masail theek karein, naye sire se banana baad mein sochein.

## Interior Designer and Architect Website: Building a Portfolio That Wins Clients in Lahore
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/architect-interior-designer-website
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: An interior designer website is mainly a portfolio: 8 to 15 strong projects with before-and-after photos, a short story for each, the services you offer, the areas you work in and an enquiry form that asks about budget and timeline. Images must load fast on phones. A portfolio site of this kind usually fits our business websites from Rs 85,500.
Key points:
- Clients judge interior designers and architects by their past projects more than by any text.
- Fewer, better-presented projects beat a long gallery of every job.
- Large photos must be optimised, or galleries become painfully slow on mobile data.
- An enquiry form that asks about property type, budget and timeline filters serious clients.
- Show genuine professional registrations where they apply, and nothing you do not hold.

Q: What should an interior designer website include?
A: A portfolio of your best eight to fifteen projects with stories and before-and-after photos, service pages, a process page with typical timelines, an about page with designers and qualifications, and a contact page with a qualifying enquiry form, WhatsApp, studio address and map.

Q: How many projects should be in a design portfolio website?
A: Usually eight to fifteen strong projects work better than a long gallery of every job. Each should have a short story covering the brief, challenge, approach and result, plus quality photos. Quality and relevance to the clients you want matter more than quantity.

Q: How do I stop my portfolio gallery loading slowly?
A: Resize photos to sensible display sizes, compress them, use modern formats such as WebP where supported, and load images further down the page only as visitors scroll. Large original photos straight from a camera are the most common cause of slow design portfolios on mobile.

Q: Should architects show their registration on their website?
A: Where it genuinely applies, yes. Architects in Pakistan register with the Pakistan Council of Architects and Town Planners, and engineers with the Pakistan Engineering Council. Showing a real registration clients can check builds trust. Never show registrations or awards you do not actually hold.

Q: What questions should an interior design enquiry form ask?
A: Property type, approximate size, area, scope of work, rough budget range and desired start date, plus name and phone number. These help you decide which enquiries to prioritise. Offer WhatsApp as an alternative and say how quickly you will respond and what happens next.

Q: Do I need client permission to show project photos?
A: Yes. Get written permission before publishing photos of a client's home or business, avoid exact addresses, keep personal items and documents out of shots, and remove photos promptly if a client later asks. Respecting privacy also reassures future clients considering your services.

Q: Interior designer ki website mein kya hona chahiye?
A: Apne behtareen 8 se 15 projects ki tasveerein aur mukhtasar kahani, services, kaam ka tareeqa, team ka taaruf aur aisa enquiry form jo budget aur waqt pooche. Tasveerein chhoti karke lagayen taake mobile par jaldi khulein. Client ki ijazat ke baghair uske ghar ki tasveer na lagayen.

URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/wedding-event-planner-website

Short answer: A wedding planner website should show past events in galleries grouped by function, such as mehndi, barat and walima, explain packages with starting prices, let couples check date availability and enquire on WhatsApp. It must load fast on phones and be ready before the 2 main wedding seasons. Most fit our business websites from Rs 85,500.
Key points:
- Couples and families decide largely from photos and videos of real events.
- Package pages with starting prices filter enquiries and save hours of calls.
- An availability check or date field in the enquiry form helps in peak season.
- WhatsApp is the main enquiry channel for most Pakistani families.
- Update the site before the busy season, not during it.

Q: What should a wedding planner website include?
A: Event galleries grouped by function such as mehndi, barat and walima, package pages with what is included and starting prices, a services page, venues you work with, genuine reviews, and an enquiry form asking for date, guest numbers, budget and WhatsApp number.

Q: Should wedding planners show package prices online?
A: Starting prices help many families decide whether to call, which saves time on both sides. Show what each package includes and what costs extra, and explain that final prices depend on guest numbers, venue and choices. Avoid hidden costs that surprise families later.

Q: How should event photos be organised on a planner's website?
A: Group them by function and style so families quickly find what matches their taste, and use a handful of strong images per event rather than hundreds. Optimise images and videos for fast loading, and get permission before publishing any family's event.

Q: When should I update my event website before wedding season?
A: Before the busy season starts, not during it. Refresh galleries and packages, prepare WhatsApp quick replies for common questions, and make sure the enquiry form asks for the event date first, so you can respond quickly to dates you can still serve.

Q: Do event planners need an availability calendar?
A: It can help during peak season by reducing enquiries for dates already booked. A simple calendar updated by your team works for many planners. Larger companies with several teams may benefit from a booking system that tracks staff, decor stock and venues together.

Q: How do I protect families' privacy on my wedding website?
A: Ask permission before publishing event photos, avoid showing guests who have not agreed, take extra care with images of women and children, and never publish family names, addresses or invitation details without consent. Remove photos promptly if a family asks.

Q: Shaadi planner ki website mein kya dikhayein?

## Photographer Website Guide: Fast Portfolio Galleries, Client Proofing and Booking Deposits
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/photographer-portfolio-website
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: A photographer website needs fast, beautiful galleries above all, organised by type such as weddings, portraits or products, plus clear packages, a booking form with date and deposit details, and private client galleries for proofing and delivery. Optimise every image for the web; 1 heavy gallery can lose visitors. Sites start from Rs 40,500.
Key points:
- Your galleries are the product; speed and presentation matter more than anything else.
- Serve web-sized, compressed images; keep full-resolution files for client delivery only.
- Watermarks deter casual copying but can distract; use them lightly.
- Private, password-protected galleries suit proofing and delivery.
- A deposit secures dates and reduces last-minute cancellations.

Q: What should a photographer website include?
A: Fast portfolio galleries organised by type, a few featured stories, clear packages with deliverables and starting prices, an about page, password-protected client galleries for proofing and delivery, and a booking form that asks for the date first and explains deposits.

Q: How do I make my photography website load faster?
A: Upload web-sized images rather than camera originals, typically around 2,000 pixels on the long side, compress them carefully, use modern formats such as WebP where supported, and load images as visitors scroll. Test on a mid-range phone using mobile data, not office Wi-Fi.

Q: Should photographers watermark website images?
A: A small, subtle watermark is a reasonable compromise for public galleries. Large watermarks distract from the work. The stronger protection is only publishing web-sized images and keeping full-resolution files for client delivery, because small web images are far less useful for printing.

Q: What are client galleries for photographers?
A: Private, password-protected galleries where clients view, select and download their photos. They are used for proofing album choices and delivering final images, replacing large file transfers over WhatsApp or USB drives. Set download expiry dates and agree in the contract how long files stay available.

Q: How should photographers handle booking deposits?
A: Explain the deposit amount that secures the date, when the balance is due and what happens if the event is cancelled or moved. Collect deposits by bank transfer or a payment gateway, and confirm bookings in writing with the date, coverage and package.

Q: Do I need permission to show client photos in my portfolio?
A: Yes. Get written permission before showing clients publicly, especially at weddings and with families or children. Many photographers include a portfolio permission clause in the contract, with an option for clients who prefer privacy. Remove images promptly if a client asks.

Q: Photographer ki website kaisi honi chahiye?
A: Tasveerein tez khulni chahiyein aur kaam ki qisam ke hisaab se alag galleries hon, jaise shaadi, portrait aur products. Packages aur shuruati qeemat, booking form jismein pehle tareekh poochi jaye, aur clients ke liye password wali private gallery rakhein. Client ki ijazat ke baghair tasveer na lagayen.

## Car Rental Website in Pakistan: Fleet Pages, Online Bookings, Deposits and ID Checks
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/car-rental-website-pakistan
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: A car rental website in Pakistan needs fleet pages with real photos and daily rates, an availability check by date, clear with-driver and self-drive options, deposit and fuel rules, and a secure way to collect ID documents. A simple site with WhatsApp booking starts from Rs 40,500; a full booking system is a web app from Rs 360,000.
Key points:
- Customers want to see the actual car, its daily rate and what is included before calling.
- Showing availability by date saves hours of WhatsApp back-and-forth.
- With-driver and self-drive rentals have different rules; present them separately.
- Deposits, fuel, mileage and late-return rules must be written plainly.
- CNIC and licence copies are sensitive and need secure handling and deletion.

Q: What should a car rental website include?
A: Fleet pages with real photos, model, year and daily rate, separate with-driver and self-drive options, availability by date, out-of-city trip rates, a clear rules page covering deposit, fuel, mileage, late return, damage and cancellation, and a booking form or system.

Q: Does a rent-a-car business need a booking system?
A: Small fleets can manage with a website showing cars, rates and rules plus a pre-filled WhatsApp button. Larger fleets benefit from a booking system that tracks vehicle availability, prevents double bookings, handles deposits, assigns drivers and sends reminders automatically, saving staff hours every week.

Q: How much does a car rental website cost in Pakistan?
A: A fleet and rules website with WhatsApp booking starts from Rs 40,500. A full booking system with availability, deposits, ID upload and driver allocation is a custom web app from Rs 360,000, depending on fleet size, features and how bookings must connect with drivers and payments.

Q: How should car rental companies handle CNIC copies online?
A: Use a secure upload over HTTPS, store files where only authorised staff can see them, and delete them after the rental and any dispute period. Never collect documents in WhatsApp groups, and explain in your privacy policy what you collect and how long you keep it.

Q: Which rental rules should be on the website?
A: Security deposit and how it is returned, fuel policy, daily mileage limits, charges for late return, damage responsibility and cancellation terms. Show them before booking and ask customers to confirm they have read them, because most rental disputes come from verbal rules.

Q: Why should a rental website show real car photos?
A: Customers worry about receiving an older or different car than the one advertised. Photographs of your actual vehicles, with honest model years and updated when cars change, build trust and reduce disputes at pick-up. Stock images of new cars can damage credibility.

Q: Rent a car ki website mein kya hona chahiye?
A: Har gaari ki asli tasveer, model, saal aur rozana kiraya, driver ke saath aur self-drive ke alag rates, tareekh ke hisaab se dastiyabi, aur deposit, fuel aur late wapsi ke saaf usool. CNIC ki copy mehfooz tareeqe se lein aur kaam khatam hone ke baad delete kar dein.

## Tuition Centre and Coaching Academy Website in Pakistan: Courses, Timetables and Admissions
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/tuition-academy-website
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: An academy website in Pakistan should list courses by class and subject, show batch timetables and campus locations, explain fees or fee ranges, and take online admission enquiries. Results and toppers should be shown only with real, checkable details and permission. A standard academy site starts from Rs 40,500; online classes need an LMS.
Key points:
- Parents and students look first for courses, timings, location and fees.
- Batch timetables kept up to date prevent many repeat phone calls.
- An online admission form with class, subject and batch speeds up enrolment.
- Show results honestly, with permission, and avoid guarantees of grades or admissions.
- Recorded lectures and tests need a learning management system, not just a website.

Q: What should an academy website include?
A: Course pages by class, board and subject, batch timetables with start dates, fees or fee ranges and payment methods, teacher profiles with permission, genuine results with consent, an online admission form, and campus addresses with maps, phone numbers and timings.

Q: How should an academy show results online?
A: Show only genuine results with the student's and parents' permission, including the exam and year, and details that can be checked where possible. Avoid guaranteed admission or grade claims, because outcomes depend on students and examining bodies, and exaggeration damages trust over time.

Q: Can parents apply for academy admission online?
A: Yes. An admission form can collect the student's class, board, subjects, preferred batch, campus and a parent's phone number. Confirm receipt on screen and by message, then send fee and joining details. Fees can be paid by bank transfer, wallet or gateway.

Q: Does an academy need an LMS or just a website?
A: A website handles information and admissions. If you teach online with recorded lectures, notes, tests and fee-based access, you also need a learning management system that controls access and tracks progress. Many academies start with a website and add an LMS later.

Q: How much does an academy website cost in Pakistan?
A: A standard academy website with course pages, timetables and an admission form starts from Rs 40,500. Multi-campus academies usually fit our business websites from Rs 85,500. A learning management system for online classes is a separate web application quoted after scoping.

Q: How do I protect students' data on an academy website?
A: Collect only the details needed for admission, use secure forms over HTTPS, never publish marks or photos without parents' consent, limit staff access to student records, and delete old enquiries on a schedule. Most students are children, so take extra care.

Q: Academy ki website mein kya hona chahiye?
A: Har class aur subject ke courses, batch ke auqaat, fees, teachers ka taaruf, asli results ijazat ke saath, online admission form aur har campus ka pata. Timetable hamesha update rakhein. Kabhi bhi guaranteed admission ya number ka daawa na karein, aur bachon ka data mehfooz rakhein.

## Furniture Website in Pakistan: Online Catalogue, Custom Orders, Advance Payments and Delivery
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/furniture-brand-online-store
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: A furniture website in Pakistan works best as a catalogue plus custom-order tool: real photos in rooms, dimensions, wood and fabric options, delivery charges by city and clear advance payment rules for made-to-order pieces. Q: What should a furniture website in Pakistan include?

Q: Should furniture stores offer cash on delivery?

Q: How can customers order custom furniture online?
A: Offer defined options for size, fabric and finish with price changes shown, or a custom request form for room measurements and photos. Confirm the final specification in writing before production starts, because changes after cutting wood or fabric are expensive.

Q: How should furniture delivery charges be shown?
A: Show charges by city or zone, whether assembly is included, and any extra charges for stairs, upper floors or long distances, along with realistic delivery windows. Large items need vans and helpers, so delivery costs more than for small parcels.

Q: Do furniture buyers still visit showrooms?
A: Many do, especially for sofas and beds. A good website supports this by showing the showroom address, map, hours and pieces on display, and by letting buyers save and share a shortlist with family members on WhatsApp before they visit in person.

Q: How much does a furniture website cost?

Q: Furniture ki website kaisi honi chahiye?

## Jewellery Website in Pakistan: Building Trust With Real Photos, Clear Pricing and Safe Payment
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/jewellery-store-website-pakistan
Updated: 2026-10-30
Short answer: A jewellery website in Pakistan must earn trust first: sharp close-up photos and short videos, honest material and purity details, a clear pricing approach, secure payment and a visible shop address. Artificial jewellery suits fixed online prices; gold pieces often use price on request because gold rates change daily. Stores start from Rs 157,500.
Key points:
- Trust is everything; buyers need to see detail and know you are a real, reachable business.
- Fixed prices suit artificial and silver jewellery; gold often needs price on request or rate-linked pricing.
- State purity, weight and materials only if accurate, and never claim certifications you do not hold.
- High-value items need secure payment options and careful, insured delivery.
- Close-up photos and short videos sell detail better than text.

Q: What should a jewellery website in Pakistan include?
A: Sharp close-up photos and short videos, accurate material, weight and purity details, a clear pricing approach, secure payment options, insured or trackable delivery for valuable pieces, a visible shop address and hours, genuine reviews, and clear exchange or buy-back policies where offered.

Q: Should gold jewellery prices be shown online?
A: Many sellers use price on request because gold rates change daily. Others show weight and making charges with the day's rate, dated clearly. Fixed prices work well for artificial and silver jewellery. Whatever you choose, explain how the final price is calculated.

Q: Can I mention hallmarking or purity on my jewellery website?
A: Only if it is accurate. State purity or karat and mention hallmarking or certificates only when the piece genuinely has them, and never use logos of testing bodies you are not associated with. Accurate descriptions reduce returns and protect your reputation.

Q: How should jewellery be delivered when sold online?
A: For low-value artificial pieces, standard courier with cash on delivery is common. For gold and high-value items, use insured, trackable delivery or store pick-up, take advance payment securely, and state clearly what happens if a parcel is lost or damaged in transit.

Q: How do I photograph jewellery for my website?
A: Take sharp macro photos showing stones, settings and finish, add a photo worn on a model or hand for scale, and film a short video showing sparkle in natural light. Use consistent backgrounds and avoid editing that changes the true colour of metal or stones.

Q: How much does a jewellery website cost?
A: A catalogue website with enquiry and appointment forms starts from Rs 85,500. An online store with secure payments, product options and delivery settings starts from Rs 157,500. The final price depends on catalogue size, how pricing is calculated and which payment integrations you need.

Q: Jewellery ki website par bharosa kaise banayein?
A: Saaf aur qareeb se li gayi tasveerein aur video, sahi wazan aur dhaat ki tafseel, dukaan ka pata aur auqaat, asli reviews aur wapsi ki policy dikhayein. Sone ki qeemat roz badalti hai, is liye price on request ya tareekh ke saath rate likhein. Jhoote certificate ka daawa kabhi na karein.

Q: What should a bakery website include?

Q: Do home bakeries in Pakistan need food registration?
